title: Light on a performer
summary: Give a producer a single performer and a real floor shadow in a controlled stage study. The same gesture reads differently with each of the three cue keys.

layout.skeleton: Compose a rehearsal view. A wide viewing aperture holds one performer in front of a folded rear plane. The matching edge-to-edge row of three cue keys and their shared readout sit directly beneath it.
layout.focus: Frame one performer reaching asymmetrically into light with a bent knee and one fully extended arm. The floor shadow continues the gesture. Keep the same performer, floor and framing in every cue.
layout.desktop: Allow a generous aperture and fill its width with the three cue keys. Anchor the technique to the same rail. Fit the performer, their shadow, the controls, and technique in the first viewport.
layout.mobile: Fit the entire gesture and enough floor beyond the performer to read their shadow. Keep all three keys and the readout in the initial viewport.
layout.rhythm: Give the aperture the visual space. Keep the keys and technique in one continuous reading surface aligned to its edges.

imagery.subject: Draw one performer with specific anatomy and an expressive reach. Keep the silver #A8AEC8 folded screen quiet behind them. Dusk washes the body and stage in tungsten #F6B96B. Static catches one side of the body in hard white and drops a long, sharp shadow. Flood outlines the dark front-facing body with blue light.
imagery.crop: Keep the complete performer and floor shadow visible at both widths. Use broad lighting and no procedural grain or supporting annotations.
imagery.fallback: Use three original stills of one performer and identical staging, with matching light, cast shadows and the readable technique.

motion.effect: Switch light, readable technique and the selected marker immediately. Fade a small selection marker alone.
motion.reduced: Change the lighting and every state together without motion.

action.instruction: Use native controls labeled Choose a cue. Keep a persistent filled selection and a separate inset focus outline. Let the keyboard choose every cue and make the matching technique and description update immediately.
action.label: Use the actual cue name

why: The fixed performer and their cast shadow let a producer judge each cue at human scale.

sources.observation: Driving the car demonstrates the creative developer's work while the visitor explores the portfolio. The site lists a map, respawn and multiple input methods.
The studio offers standard Work and Connect navigation alongside an optional themed command interface.

credit: Original light study inspired by the interactive demonstrations of Bruno Simon and ToyFight. Use only original artwork.

title: Read the floodwall
summary: Make a single waterfront scene where the water meets a stenciled flood gauge. A selectable elevation changes the gauge, the landmarks and the plain-text closure report.

layout.skeleton: Give the reader an immediate answer next to three level choices, then one wide waterfront scene with a foreground stenciled height gauge. Place the actual crossings in the scene. Leave out the separate legend and inset charts.
layout.focus: Let the water sit against a vertical gauge painted on the floodwall. Water covers the lowest gauge marks. The actual crossing shapes change visually as they close.
layout.desktop: Run the complete scene across the main reading width at no more than 415 px tall. Keep the result and level choices close together above it and fit all of it in 900 px. Make the selected elevation the visual anchor of both.
layout.mobile: Put the result and level choices above the waterfront in the first viewport. Compose a separate compact frame around the gauge and largest landmark shapes. Set the 2 m, 4 m and 6 m gauge marks in legible HTML at 17 px or larger and align them to the painted wall.
layout.rhythm: Put visual weight on the paint and concrete meeting the water. Keep the surrounding type and controls quiet and readable.

imagery.subject: Create a bold editorial image from broad concrete and tidal green planes. Set the floodwall in limestone with wet stone #7FABB2 around the water. Use brass #E0AC44 for closure markers. Cover the path with water when it closes, show the stopped ferry floating rather than submerged, and close the footbridge with a visible marker.
imagery.crop: Keep the full wall gauge, the changing waterline and the crossing silhouettes in the first viewport at both widths. Leave small lettering out of the drawing.
imagery.fallback: Keep the readable gauge with the current elevation and the complete written closure report. Reduce scene detail before reducing the text.

motion.effect: Move the waterline as one gesture. Change the crossing indicators and the complete text together.
motion.reduced: Use the immediate new level and matching list without the marker animation.

action.instruction: Use three named level controls with a visible persistent selected state. Update the current level, waterline and cumulative text outcome together. Preserve all supplied facts and the visible keyboard focus.
action.label: Use each supplied level and its units

why: The stenciled gauge attaches the level to a physical place. The changing conditions and the readable report make the cumulative closures clear.

sources.observation: The ascent orders the exhibits by real altitude. The Kármán line is one of the named markers.
Depth provides the organizing scale of an explorable ocean story.

credit: Original waterfront study inspired by Neal Agarwal's single-axis stories.
